criteria.criterion: A new file docs/design/parallel-jobs.md exists and states the problem: jobs run one at a time, and queued jobs must be run by hand.
criteria.evidence: Section 1 says `athena go <job>` runs exactly one job, and that a user with several proposed or queued jobs must start each by hand. It cites main.rs and run.rs.

criteria.criterion: The doc specifies the concurrency model (threads vs. separate processes), the worker bound and its default, and how the existing job and repository locks are reused.
criteria.evidence: §4.1 compares threads, child processes, async and a daemon; it recommends threads and names processes as the fallback. §4.2 sets parallel.max_workers / --jobs N with default 2, labeled an estimate, plus a ceiling. §4.3 covers per-worker try_lock_job, the repository lock taken only during landing, and the lock order. The lock claims match state.rs:68-82.

criteria.criterion: The doc specifies how the kill switch (refuse_if_stopped) and per-job budgets apply to every parallel job, and how failure is isolated so one job's failure or lock conflict does not abort the others.
criteria.evidence: §5.1: refuse_if_stopped is checked at launch and by each worker, and is never cached. §5.2: budgets stay per job, with the worst-case spend stated. §5.3: a results table (locked, refused, error), with errors and panics caught at the worker boundary and a lock conflict treated as a result.

criteria.criterion: The doc specifies the CLI surface (multi-job and --all form, per-job result lines, exit codes with single-job behavior unchanged) and how conflicting jobs end stale or blocked, never merged silently.
criteria.evidence: §6.1 gives the forms and the --all set, which matches the match in run.rs:120-157. §6.2 covers per-job lines and the JSON array. §6.3 gives exit codes: single-job unchanged; multi-job 1 > 2 > 0. §7 says conflicts end stale, failed or blocked, with no automatic merge.

criteria.criterion: The doc has a section on landing each parallel job as its own branch/PR, designed and explicitly marked not built, and consistent with docs/design/native-pr-landing.md and docs/design/squash-chain-landing.md.
criteria.evidence: §8 is marked 'Not built' and depends on native-pr-landing.md, whose status is 'proposed (D72)' (verified at line 3). It follows that doc on branch naming (§5.1 step 1), stale handling (§5.1 step 6), no force push (§5.2) and M30 for squash. It keeps one job per PR, so the multi-job squash from the squash-chain design never arises.

criteria.criterion: The doc lists alternatives considered with reasons for rejection, open questions for the reviewer, and a build plan splitting later review and implementation jobs. It states that the independent review is pending.
criteria.evidence: §9 lists alternatives A-F, each with a reason for rejection, and §4.1 covers the model alternatives. §11 has seven open questions. §10 splits the build into review, spike, implementation, tests, docs and PR-landing jobs. The status line and §10 both say the review is pending.

criteria.criterion: No Rust source, Cargo, config, CI, README, CHANGELOG, or docs/design/reviews files change. A decisions.md entry is deferred to the build job.
criteria.evidence: The diff touches only docs/design/parallel-jobs.md. §10 item 5 and §12 defer the decisions.md entry to a later job.

criteria.criterion: Run `git status` and `git diff --stat`: only docs/design/parallel-jobs.md is added or modified. Run `cargo fmt --check`: it passes.
criteria.evidence: git status: working tree clean. git diff --stat HEAD~1: only docs/design/parallel-jobs.md, 316 insertions. cargo fmt --check exited 0 with no output.

findings.summary: The doc says the workers spend 'against a shared budget', which contradicts its own per-job budget design.
findings.evidence: §4.2 says each worker runs agents that 'cost money against a shared budget (section 5)'. §5.2 says budgets stay per job and are not pooled, and makes a run-level cap an open question.

findings.summary: Some line-number citations will drift as the code changes.
findings.evidence: It cites things like 'run.rs line 116' and 'manage.rs line 80'. I checked run.rs:116, and it is correct today.

request_reading_mismatch: None in the reading. The brief's "Expected deliverables" list includes edits to athena-v0.md, decisions.md and CHANGELOG.md, which contradicts the reading, criterion 7 and the out-of-scope list. The candidate followed the reading and criteria, which is correct.
summary: The change adds one file, docs/design/parallel-jobs.md, and changes nothing else. The doc covers every part of the accepted reading: the problem; a threads-versus-processes model with a recommendation and a fallback; a worker bound with a default of 2, labeled an estimate; reuse of the job and repository locks with a lock order; per-worker kill-switch checks; budgets kept per job; failure isolation by result type; a multi-job and --all CLI with exit codes that leave single-job behavior unchanged; conflicts ending stale or blocked; a section on per-job branch/PR landing marked not built; alternatives; open questions; and a build plan that says the review is pending. I spot-checked the code claims against the source and they match: run.rs:111 and :116-117, state.rs try_lock_job and lock_repository, land_or_block at run.rs:1156 with Refusal::Moved retries, and lib.rs:132. The claims about native-pr-landing.md (status "proposed (D72)", §5.1 step 6, §5.2 no force push) and squash-chain-landing.md §4 also match. I ran git status, git diff --stat and cargo fmt --check: the tree is clean, only the doc is in the diff, and fmt passes. I found one minor wording slip in the doc.
